interactions.summary: Jiang restates Beatrice's pedagogical point: heaven has no literal time or space, so temporal and spatial staging is added only so human minds can understand it.

A student reads Beatrice's explanation that scripture and church imagery anthropomorphize the divine for human understanding, then introduces Timaeus's doctrine that souls return to their original star.

Jiang turns Timaeus into a classroom problem: if souls simply return to their original home, what is the point of earthly life; a student answers that experience can shape and enlighten us, but Jiang says that answer still fails under Timaeus because it leaves the soul fixed in the same heavenly slot, unlike Dante's model of ascent.
A student pushes the logic into a materialist challenge: if the afterlife position is fixed, why not maximize earthly pleasures instead.

claims.claim: Jiang says the heavenly scene must be translated into time and space for human understanding even though heaven itself does not literally operate under those conditions.
Jiang frames Timaeus as a soul-world doctrine in which souls come with a purpose and return to the same place after death, a view that threatens to make earthly action seem pointless.

Jiang says the student's answer about earthly growth still does not solve Timaeus's problem because, on that model, the soul remains stuck in the same heavenly place after death, whereas Dante's view allows real ascent.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compresses Beatrice's pedagogy into a stark method claim: only by adding time and space can we understand what is happening in heaven.
signature_moments.source_phrase: only by adding in time and space can we truly understand what's going on
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the packet's core move from metaphysics into a humanly intelligible teaching image.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns Timaeus into an existential taunt: if you just end where you started, who cares what you do here?
signature_moments.source_phrase: what is the point of life then
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This question drives the contrast between a static soul-return cosmology and Dante's upward moral drama.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The Platonic source Beatrice cites as teaching that a soul returns to the same star from which it originally descended into embodied life.
Jiang's shorthand for the pre-earthly and post-earthly realm from which souls come and to which they return in the Timaeus model.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet sharpens Jiang's contrast between Timaeus and Dante: Timaeus leaves the soul returning to its original station, while Dante is framed as permitting genuine ascent.
